  Windows stores a symlink's target with backslashes, so a link such as a macOS framework's
  `Chromium Embedded Framework` → `Versions/A/…` never matched the `/`-separated target recorded at
  install, and the install failed with "did not verify after install". The check now compares the
  targets in the recorded form.
- **`@denext/backend`: an Edge Function stuck in synchronous code no longer takes the function
  down.** A timeout (or a client going away) only asked the worker to abort the request, so a
  function busy in a loop such as `while (true) {}` kept its worker at 100 % CPU and every later
  call to it timed out. The worker now acknowledges an abort; one that does not within a second
  is terminated and replaced, the requests it was still serving fail with `504 WORKER_TIMEOUT`,
  and the next call starts on a fresh worker.
- **`denext storage cp -r` keeps every download inside the destination folder.** An object key
  written by other tooling (`a/../../x`, an absolute path, a drive letter, a backslash) could
  place a file outside the folder being copied into. Such a key now refuses the whole copy before
  anything is written.
- **A generated Dockerfile on a non-default port now listens on it.** The image's `CMD` was
  `deno task start -- --port N`; `deno task` forwards the literal `--`, so `denext start` took
  `--port` as passthrough and stayed on 3000. The Dockerfile now sets `ENV PORT=N` (which
  `start` reads) and keeps the bare `CMD ["deno", "task", "start"]`.
- **`denext generate docker`: the MinIO bucket bootstrap no longer fails on first start.** The
  image restarts its server once after its first boot, after the health check has already passed,
  so `minio-init` could find nothing listening ("connection refused"). The bootstrap now retries.
- **The SAML metadata background refresh no longer starts during a build.** The timer
  (`saml.metadataRefresh`) now starts only when serving (`dev` / `start`), not in `denext build`
  or export.
- **`/auth/v1` phone-factor challenges spend the user's SMS budget, not the factor's**:
  unenrolling and re-enrolling a phone factor no longer starts a fresh send budget.
- **`/auth/v1` `/resend` for an SMS confirmation answers `over_sms_send_rate_limit`** past its
  budget (it answered `over_email_send_rate_limit`).
- **`inMemoryAuthAdapter()` keeps one live verification token per address and purpose**, as the
  SQL adapters do: issuing a new one retires the older, and a token is consumed only when its
  hash matches (compared in constant time).
- **The toolchain re-exec reads the project's `deno.json`.** A project task that runs the CLI from
  JSR (`deno run -A jsr:@denext/denext@<v>/cli build`) found the project's config from the working
  directory, but the copy it re-ran on denext's Deno toolchain started from the module's https URL,
  which discovers no config, so a `denext.config.ts` import that only the import map names failed
  with `Import "…" not a dependency`. The child now resolves the config its parent resolved: an
  explicit `--config`, none after `--no-config`, else the file the parent's own discovery found (a
  workspace member's included), together with the parent's `--lock`, `--import-map`,
  `--node-modules-dir`, `--vendor`, `--frozen` and `--min-dep-age` flags. A compiled
  executable's pinned-denext child and `denext ui`'s verb runs follow the same rule.
- **A fresh `denext create` project is `deno fmt`- and `deno lint`-clean.** Every template and
  feature (`--template minimal`, `--tailwind`, `--src-dir`, `--desktop`, `--capacitor`, `--fallow`,
  `--mcp`, …) writes its README, pages, stylesheet, `AGENTS.md` and packaging / coverage scripts
  the way `deno fmt`'s defaults lay them out, so `deno fmt --check` changes nothing. A test
  scaffolds each combination and runs both.
- **`denext toolchain status` under the compiled executable** no longer says it is "running on
  deno 2.9.7" (the Deno embedded in the executable, which runs only the CLI itself): it says
  denext runs every command on the toolchain, or on the `deno` on `PATH` with
  `DENEXT_DENO=stock`, and that a missing toolchain downloads on the first denext command.
- **Running a project verb no longer reports it as an unknown command on a loaded machine.**
  `denext <verb>` discovered the project's `commands:` / plugin verbs under the 1.5 s budget meant
  for listings, so a config import slowed by a cold cache or a busy CPU dropped the verb silently
  (`denext: unknown command "seed"`). Dispatch now waits up to 30 s, and when discovery still falls
  short — a hung plugin `setup`, a config that throws — the error says why.
- The Deno Desktop runtime's Deno version check accepts denext's Deno toolchain
  (`2.9.7-denext.N` is Deno 2.9.7).
- **`denext create`'s least-privilege `deno task start` serves the built app.** It failed with
  `NotCapable: Requires run access` on every scaffolded app: `denext start` rebuilt the
  stylesheets and re-ran itself under a CSS import map (a second `deno`), and an app with no
  Flight route re-crawled its import graph with a `deno info` child. The build now points every
  server module's stylesheet import at its shim in the server copies and records the crawled
  boundary, so `start` spawns nothing and needs no `--allow-run` (a SPA's `start` skips the CSS
  step too). A next-compat build, or a project moved since its build, still takes the old path.
- **Per-address limits key on the same client through a basePath, a config rewrite and a custom
  middleware runner's rewrite.** The request rebuilt for the new URL lost the recorded socket peer, so
  `rateLimit()`'s default key put every client of such a route in one `unknown` bucket and
  `clientIp()` answered `undefined` there.
- **`ipBucket()` (every per-address limit) buckets a NAT64 address (`64:ff9b::/96`) and an
  IPv4-compatible one (`::198.51.100.7`) by the IPv4 address it carries**, as it already did for
  an IPv4-mapped one, instead of putting every such client in one shared `/64`.

### Security

- **A forged `Host` can no longer reach a cached page's metadata URLs (web cache poisoning).**
  Without `canonicalOrigin`, the `og:image` an `opengraph-image` file adds and the automatic
  hreflang / canonical links took their origin from the request's `Host` (or a trusted
  `X-Forwarded-Host`). Absolute metadata URLs now resolve against `canonicalOrigin` (or
  `DENEXT_CANONICAL_ORIGIN`), else the page's `metadataBase`, as in Next.js. Without either,
  a page the ISR cache may store (`revalidate`, `force-static`) keeps `og:image` relative and
  omits hreflang / canonical, where before the page was turned dynamic. A per-request page
  still uses the request's origin and is sent `no-store`. A `generateSitemaps` sitemap index
  built on a `Host`-derived origin is now sent `private, no-store` too. Production logs one
  warning when no stable origin is configured.
  Hardening of the new `/auth/v1` API (unreleased) and the user store it shares with `denextAuth()`:
- **No password set before an address was proven survives its first proof.** A magic link, an
  email or SMS one-time code, a recovery link or an invite that first confirms an account's
  address now retires everything set up on it before: the password, second factors, passkeys,
  bearer API tokens and every session (token and cookie). Only the account's own sign-up
  confirmation, bound to the password that sign-up chose, keeps it. Previously a magic link into
  an account someone else had registered with the address kept that person's password. An
  anonymous user's address change keeps only the password it held when the change was requested,
  and an anonymous user can't set a password without an email or phone (GoTrue's rule). An OAuth
  provider's verified email marks the stored address verified only when it is the same address,
  and an `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking` link onto an unconfirmed account clears that account
  first.
- **Account changes need `aal2` once a user has a verified factor.** `PUT /user` refuses a
  password, email or phone change from a session below `aal2` (`401 insufficient_aal`, as GoTrue
  does), and linking or unlinking an identity needs `aal2` too. A session that still owes its
  second factor is refused by the account endpoints (`403 insufficient_aal`); it can still read
  the user, finish MFA and sign out.
- **Bans and password changes reach denextAuth.** A banned user can't sign in through denextAuth's
  own routes, and a ban ends every session, cookie sessions in the `sessionStore` included. A
  password change through `PUT /user` ends the user's other sessions of both kinds; an admin
  password change or user deletion ends all of them.
- **`session.user.emailVerified` of an `/auth/v1` access token comes from the stored user.** It was
  read from `user_metadata`, which the user can write; the token's `user_metadata.email_verified`
  / `phone_verified` now always carry the stored flags.
- **SAML SSO trust model.** An IdP speaks only for its provider's email domains: an address
  outside them is never bound to an account (refused, `email_address_not_authorized`, for a
  provider stored through the admin API). A first SSO sign-in no longer takes over an existing
  account with the same email (`email_exists`, as in GoTrue) unless a config-declared provider
  sets the new `linkExistingAccounts`. SSO sign-up honours `disableSignup` and the new per-provider
  `allowSignUp`, and SSO users get no `email` identity.
- **A ban refuses every token while it lasts.** A banned user's bearer API tokens, native access
  and refresh tokens and `/auth/v1` access tokens are refused at each use (`requireBearer`,
  `verifyApiToken`, `auth()`, `resolveIdentity()`, `GET /user`), not only through the revocation
  a ban performs, so a token that revocation missed is dead too; the ban's end restores them.
- **A stateless pending-MFA cookie can't finish the step-up after a ban or an eviction.** Without
  a `sessionStore` a pending cookie can't be revoked, so `/mfa`, `/mfa/enroll`, `/mfa/confirm`,
  `/mfa/challenge`, the passkey step-up and `pendingMfaSession()` refuse it when its user is
  banned or deleted, or when the account's address was first proven after it signed in.
- **SSO users' credentials belong to the IdP.** `PUT /user` refuses an SSO user's password, email
  or phone change, or a reauthentication nonce (`422 user_sso_managed`, as in GoTrue), and an SSO
  user's identities are its SSO identities only (no synthesized `email` identity), so its last
  one can't be unlinked.
- **SSO users sign in through their identity provider only.** A magic link, an email or SMS
  one-time code, a password, a recovery link or a resend for an SSO user's email or phone — on
  `/auth/v1` and through `magicLink()`, `emailOtp()`, `phoneOtp()`, `credentials()` and
  `{basePath}/reset` alike — now answers exactly as for an unknown address and sends nothing (as
  GoTrue's lookups exclude SSO users); before, any of them signed an SSO user in without the
  IdP, past its MFA, policies and deprovisioning. A sign-up for its address is answered as for a
  registered one and creates no second account. A code or reset link issued before an account
  became an SSO user signs nobody in. An OAuth, native or `id_token` sign-in never links onto an
  SSO user by email (`account_not_linked` / `email_exists`), even with
  `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking`. An SSO user can't register a passkey (`422
  validation_failed` on `/auth/v1`, `403 sso_user` on `{basePath}/passkey/register*`), a passkey
  from before signs it in nowhere, and linking an identity to it needs a session its IdP started
  (`422 user_sso_managed`). The admin API's `generate_link` answers `user_not_found` for
  `recovery` and the email-change links and `email_exists` for `magiclink`, `signup` and
  `invite` (GoTrue would create a second account there), and `POST /invite` is `email_exists`.
  Being an SSO user now follows the stored `app_metadata.provider` alone (`sso:<id>`, set by its
  first SAML sign-in), so linking or unlinking another identity no longer changes it; an existing
  account an IdP was linked to (`linkExistingAccounts`) is not an SSO user and keeps its other
  sign-in methods.
- **An SSO user's sessions are the ones its identity provider started.** A session of an SSO user
  that no SAML sign-in started — one from a password, code, link, passkey or OAuth sign-in made
  before the account became an SSO user, or before such sign-ins were refused — is now refused at
  use (`403 session_not_found`) and at refresh (`refresh_token_not_found`, its session revoked) on
  `/auth/v1`; a session that stepped up with MFA after a SAML sign-in keeps working, and a token
  issued to an OAuth client is unaffected. No such session is started any more either: a sign-in
  through an identity linked to an SSO user answers `422 user_sso_managed` on `/auth/v1`, and
  denextAuth refuses it (`AccountNotLinkedError`). denextAuth's native sessions of an SSO user are
  refused at use and revoked at refresh, and its cookie sessions end when they are next due to
  slide (`session.updateAge`). The admin API no longer changes whether a user is an SSO user:
  `app_metadata.provider` is kept as stored when an update would make a user an SSO user, stop one
  being one or move it to another provider, and `POST /admin/users` never creates one (GoTrue's
  `is_sso_user` is not admin-writable). `GET /reauthenticate` for an SSO user answers
  `422 user_sso_managed` and sends nothing (`PUT /user` refuses its nonce anyway). A SAML provider
  with `linkExistingAccounts` never links onto an SSO user another provider signed up
  (`email_exists`).
- **An admin-generated sign-up link keeps the admin's password.** `generate_link` with
  `type: "signup"` and a `password` binds the code to that password, so confirming it no longer
  retires the password as a foreign one (GoTrue's behaviour).
- **SAML metadata endpoints must be `https:`.** A SingleSignOnService / SingleLogoutService URL
  with another scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`) refuses the metadata, and `/auth/v1` refuses a
  plaintext one (loopback `http:` only under `dangerouslyAllowInsecureProviders`) at registration,
  at a refresh and at use, so the URL handed to the browser is always an HTTPS page.
- **`@denext/backend` Edge Functions: `SUPABASE_URL` never comes from a request's `Host`.** With
  neither `functions.url` nor a `SUPABASE_URL` env var, a function's worker took `SUPABASE_URL`
  from the first request that started it and kept it for its whole life, beside
  `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. One request with a forged `Host` after a start, restart or edit
  pointed every later `createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY)` at another host,
  sending it the service key. The default is now the app's `canonicalOrigin` (or
  `DENEXT_CANONICAL_ORIGIN`) plus its `basePath`, else the address the server listens on as this
  machine reaches it (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`); with none of them known, functions get no
  `SUPABASE_URL` and a warning says so.
- **`@denext/backend` storage under SQL-RLS: a write is judged against the object as it is when
  it lands.** An upload, copy, move or TUS upload by a request's user was checked by a rolled-back
  dry run and then written as the service role once its bytes were in. So an upsert that passed
  while the path was free could replace an object someone else created there in the meantime,
  even though their `update` policy would refuse it. A slow body kept that window open; a TUS
  upload kept it open for up to a day. The row is now written under the caller's role, in one
  transaction with the current row locked, and the bytes wait in a staging area until that write
  is allowed. A move takes the destination's name before it copies any bytes. A signed upload
  token minted by a policy-checked caller (`/object/upload/sign`, signed TUS,
  `createSignedUploadUrl`) is pinned to the object's version when it was signed: if the object
  has changed since, the upload is a `409`.
- **`@denext/backend` storage: a client's direct upload reaches the object only when it
  completes.** The URLs `createSignedUploadUrl` and the sign route's `upload` op hand out (an S3
  presigned PUT, presigned multipart parts, or the fs driver's signed PUT) wrote the client's
  bytes straight to the object's key. The size, type and pin checks ran later, at completion. So
  bytes the completion would refuse, or an upload never completed, replaced what was stored
  there. The URLs now point at a staging place (`.denext-staging/<bucket>/<version>`). The
  completion checks the staged bytes, then writes the row and moves the bytes to the key together
  (`409` when a pinned object has changed since signing). An abandoned upload's staged bytes, or
  its incomplete multipart upload, are swept once its completion window closes.
- **`@denext/backend` storage: emptying a bucket under SQL-RLS deletes only what the caller may
  delete.** `POST /bucket/<id>/empty` purged every noncurrent version and delete marker as the
  service role. Now each one is deleted under the caller's policies, as live objects already were.
- **`@denext/backend` storage: the SQLite metadata store matches a `list-v2` prefix
  case-sensitively.** SQLite's `LIKE` ignores ASCII case, so a listing scoped to `alice/` also
  returned `ALICE/…` and `Alice/…`. Postgres was not affected.
- **`@denext/backend` realtime: an update's full old row reaches only subscribers who could see
  the row.** With `old: "full"`, a raw `postgres_changes` subscriber received `old_record` in full
  even when the row only just entered their view (a row handed to them), which exposed its
  previous contents. On a table with row-level security on, or not known to be off, the old row now
  goes only to a subscriber who could see the row before the change, and only with the first
  change of a burst. Everyone else gets the key alone, which is what Supabase sends under
  row-level security. Tables with row-level security off still send it to every subscriber.
- **`@denext/backend` vault: `updateSecret()` with an uppercase id no longer destroys the
  secret.** The id matched the row (`::uuid` ignores case), but the new ciphertext was bound to
  the caller's spelling while every reader binds Postgres's lowercase `id::text`, so the secret
  could never be read again. Secrets are now sealed under the id the database returns, the
  additional data uses the canonical form of a UUID, and the write is checked to land on that
  row.
- **A typed-API batch item and a server-side typed-API self-call keep the client's
  `rateLimitHeader` address.** The sub-request copied only an allowlist of the parent's headers,
  so with `rateLimitHeader` set behind a loopback proxy each item had no address to limit on and
  `rateLimit()` skipped it: the batch endpoint bypassed every per-route limit. The header the app
  names is now inherited from the parent (a caller's extra header cannot replace it).
- **Behaviour note for direct LAN / VPN deployments:** since the change above that aligns the
  `denextAuth` per-IP budgets with the limit-address rule, those budgets (sign-in start, session
  read, the IP-wide buckets) are skipped for ANY untrusted loopback/private socket peer, not only
  one that sends `x-forwarded-for`. Where those peers are the real clients, set
  `rateLimitLocalAddresses: true` to budget each by its own address. The credentials limiter's
  per-identifier key applies either way.

### Breaking (4.0)

These are what moving a 3.x app to 4.0 involves. This section is the record.

- **Project verbs run on denext's Deno toolchain.** `dev`, `build`, `export`, `start`, `test`,
  `check`, `job`, `doctor` and the other verbs that run project code re-run themselves on the
  pinned `2.9.7-denext.N` Deno, downloaded and SHA-256-verified into `<DENO_DIR>/denext-deno/` on
  first need, so the Deno your code runs on is no longer the one that started the CLI. A launcher
  that denies `--allow-run`, or a sandbox without network on first use, stays on stock Deno (one
  warning); `DENEXT_DENO=stock` opts out.
- **First-party plugins need their 4.0 releases.** Each plugin's 4.0-compatible release requires
  denext 4.0, and the releases built for 3.x don't work with it: `@denext/backend` 0.4,
  `@denext/content-collections` 0.5, `@denext/effect` 0.2, `@denext/graphql` 0.3, `@denext/htmx`
  2.1, `@denext/openapi` 0.4, `@denext/pages-router` 0.12, `@denext/react-router` 0.3.
  `denext upgrade` moves the denext pin, the CLI tasks and these plugins together.
- **No `npm:esbuild`.** denext runs the esbuild 0.25.5 binary its toolchain ships (or the
  verified `@esbuild/<platform>` one), and the framework deps a local-path migration copies no
  longer include `esbuild`: an app that imports esbuild itself adds its own `deno.json` entry.
- **`@denext/backend`: `db()` scopes every query with the request's identity**
  (`resolveIdentity()`): with `backend({ supabase })` keys, the secret key runs as `service_role`
  with no row-level security, and a refused credential is an `IdentityError` (401).
- **`@denext/backend` storage:** `listBuckets` for anon and signed-in callers is an empty list
  and `getBucket` is `Bucket not found` (they were `403`); a bucket's `authorize` receives the
  request's `identity`, and a bucket created at runtime (or declared without `authorize`) is
  decided by `storage.authorize`, else open only to the service role; the size refusal reads "The
  object exceeded the maximum allowed size".
- **`@denext/backend` auto-REST:** `readRestCatalog(sql, schemas, tables)` takes a list of
  schemas and returns the whole catalog, `generateRestTypes(catalog)` takes the catalog alone,
  and the client's `range()` sends `offset` / `limit` instead of a `Range` header.
- **`denext generate docker`'s Postgres publishes no host port** unless `--expose-db`
  (`127.0.0.1:5432`).
- **`denext db` is a core verb**, no longer contributed by `@denext/backend`.
- **A TOTP secret kept in a pre-4.0 user's MFA record moves into the factor store** the first time
  the user's factors are read (no key needed). Keep a database backup from before the upgrade if
  you may need to roll back to 3.x.

- **`denext task` is Deno's `deno task`.** `denext task <name> [args…]` runs a `deno.json` /
  `package.json` task on denext's Deno toolchain, every argument verbatim. Inside it every `deno`
  is the toolchain: Deno's task shell runs its own executable for a `deno …` step, and a script or
  tool the task starts finds that binary as `deno` on `PATH` — through the toolchain's own cache
  directory, or a directory holding only a `deno` link to it — with every other `PATH` lookup
  (node, npm, python) unchanged, and no change at all when `PATH` already finds it. A leading global
  flag goes after the subcommand (`denext --config deno.json task p` → `deno task --config
  deno.json p`; `denext -A main.ts` → `deno run -A main.ts`); `--verbose` is denext's alone.
  `denext ui`'s Tasks page runs a task the same way.
- **Background and scheduled tasks are now jobs**, end to end, with no aliases: `denext job <name>
  | --list | --history | --clear-history`; the `tasks/` directory is `jobs/`; `defineTask` →
  `defineJob`, `runTask` → `runJob`, `registerTask` / `getTask` / `isTask` / `taskNames` →
  `registerJob` / `getJob` / `isJob` / `jobNames`; the types `Task`, `TaskContext`,
  `TaskDefinition`, `TaskRetry`, `TaskBackoff`, `TaskRunRecord`, `TasksConfig`,
  `TaskHistoryConfig` and `TaskHistory*` → `Job…`; `sqliteTaskHistoryStore` /
  `postgresTaskHistoryStore` → `sqliteJobHistoryStore` / `postgresJobHistoryStore`; config
  `scheduledTasks` → `scheduledJobs` and `tasks: { history, historyMaxRuns }` → `jobs: { … }`;
  the history file `.denext/tasks.db` → `.denext/jobs.db` (and the Postgres store's `task_runs`
  table → `job_runs`, a run's `task` field → `job`, and `denext job --list --json`'s `tasks` → `jobs`); `denext generate task` → `denext generate
  job`, and `generate migration` / `generate seed` write `jobs/migrate.ts` / `jobs/seed.ts`. A
  config that still sets `tasks` or `scheduledTasks` fails to load, naming the new key. The docs
  page moved to [/docs/jobs](https://denext.dev/docs/jobs).
- **`denext info <module>`** is Deno's `deno info` (its flags pass through); `denext info [dir]`
  keeps printing denext's environment and project facts. Deno's cache info: `denext deno info`.
- **`denext audit` also runs `deno audit`** (Deno's audit flags — `--level`, `--ignore`,
  `--ignore-unfixable`, `--socket`, `--fix`, `--lock`, … — forwarded) and exits non-zero when
  either half fails. Deno's half needs the network (the advisory services) and reads the
  lockfile, so an offline CI step or a project without `deno.lock` that ran `denext audit` before
  now fails or changes its result: pass `--skip-deno-audit` for denext's checks only.
- A forwarding verb (`test`, `lint`, `fmt`, `check`, `add`, `remove`, `update`) keeps a literal
  `--` in what it hands Deno, so `denext test a.test.ts -- --seed 1` gives the script its own
  arguments, and hands back `--quiet` (and `--json` to `lint`), which denext parses as global
  flags.

### Notes

- **How denext's Deno build is kept current**: how the `2.9.7-denext.N` toolchain tracks Deno
  releases and takes fixes between them, how each denext release pins and verifies one build, and
  how the first command bootstraps it. See
  [denext's Deno toolchain › Notes](https://denext.dev/docs/toolchain#notes-how-denexts-deno-build-is-kept-current).

## [3.4.16] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- **`clientIpForLimits({ bucket: true })`** answers the address's limit bucket instead of the
  address: an IPv4 address as it is, an IPv6 one normalised to its `/64` prefix
  (`2001:db8:1:2::/64`), the key the framework's own per-address limits use. Without the option
  it answers the address, as before.

### Changed

- **denext pins Deno Desktop runtime 2.9.7-denext.14** (deno `5c7842ee`, laufey `09ad1b6`, API
  47), a maintenance release. A child the app starts from its own executable (a module sidecar's
  `spawnSelf`, `child_process.fork()`) gets a stdout of its own: the runtime prints its launch
  messages (`Runtime loaded successfully from: …`, `Runtime started`) on stderr, so `spawnSelf` no
  longer strips them, and a spawn of your own from `childCommand` starts clean too. Such a child
  never applies or rolls back a staged full-app update (only the app's own launch does), and a fork
  the runtime authorized (an IPC channel and its per-launch worker token) needs no `--allow-run`
  for the executable's path. A dynamic `import()` of a module not loaded before puts the
  importer's `AsyncLocalStorage` / `AsyncContext` back once it is evaluated: the next `Deno.serve`
  request no longer sees the previous request's store. On Windows a passkey request whose window
  closes at once now frees the one-ceremony slot. Still needs at least denext.9. Docs:
  [Deno Desktop runtime › Headless workers and forks of the app](https://denext.dev/docs/desktop-runtime#headless-workers-and-forks-of-the-app).

### Fixed

- **`@denext/backend` realtime: a `timestamptz` key matches across `TimeZone` settings.**
  `to_jsonb()` formats a `timestamptz` in the session's `TimeZone`, so a write from a session in
  one zone notified `2026-01-01T22:04:05-05:00` while a subscriber's re-read in another spelled
  the same key `2026-01-02T03:04:05+00:00`: the change was dropped, and a seeded key never matched
  its delete. Migration `backend_realtime_0002` replaces the trigger function so that a key column
  whose catalog type is `timestamptz` is sent in UTC (`2026-01-02T03:04:05`), and the re-read and
  seed queries spell such a key the same way (`to_jsonb(k AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') #>> '{}'`). Other key
  types are unchanged. With `migrate: false`, re-run `realtimeSetupSql()`.

### Security

- **`rateLimit()` no longer turns into one site-wide bucket behind an undeclared proxy.** Its
  default key was the client address even when that was a loopback, private, link-local or
  unique-local socket peer with no trusted forwarded hop — a reverse proxy every visitor shares —
  so the `max`th request across the whole site rate-limited everyone. The default key now follows
  `clientIpForLimits()`'s rule: such a request is not limited (a loopback request in local
  development included), and the server warns once, naming the address and
  `rateLimit({ trustForwardedHeaders: true })` (or a custom `key`). A custom `key` still applies;
  a public peer, or a trusted proxy's last hop, is limited as before — and an IPv6
  address now counts against its `/64`, so rotating within the allocation (or re-spelling the
  address) no longer opens a fresh bucket.
- **Per-address limits no longer lump every IPv4 client of a dual-stack listener together.** An
  IPv4-mapped address (`::ffff:198.51.100.7`, how a server listening on `::` reports an IPv4
  client) was bucketed by its `/64`, which every IPv4 client shares, so the auth limiters and
  `live.limits.maxConnectionsPerIp` treated all of them as one client. Such an address now counts
  as the IPv4 address it carries.
- **`@denext/backend` realtime: the signed-out quota is per IPv6 `/64`.** It keyed the raw
  address, so an IPv6 client could rotate through its `/64` for a fresh quota per connection. It
  now keys `clientIpForLimits({ bucket: true })`.

## [3.4.15] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- **`@denext/backend`: auto-REST.** `backend({ postgres, rest: { schema?, tables?, basePath?,
  maxRows?, maxBodyBytes?, statementTimeout? } })` serves the schema's tables PostgREST-style
  under `/rest/v1/<table>` — only those the `anon` / `authenticated` roles hold a privilege on, read
  from the catalog at startup (and on a miss under `denext dev`). `GET` / `HEAD` with `select=`
  (columns only), filters (`eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `like`, `ilike`, `is`, `in`, each
  behind an optional `not.`), `order=`, `limit` / `offset` / `Range` capped at `maxRows`,
  `Prefer: count=exact` → `Content-Range`, and `Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json`; `POST`
  (an object or an array), and `PATCH` / `DELETE` that refuse a request without a filter, with
  `Prefer: return=representation`. Every statement runs through `db()` (the request's user, or
  `anon`) under a per-request `statement_timeout`; identifiers come only from the catalog and every
  value is a typed `$n` parameter (a body is one `$n::json` expanded by `json_populate_record(set)`).
  Errors are PostgREST-shaped `{ code, message, details, hint }` with SQLSTATEs mapped (`23505` →
  409, `42501` → 403, `57014` → 504). Cookie-carrying cross-site writes are refused (the `csrf()`
  rule). `from("table")` / `restClient()` from `@denext/backend/client` build the requests
  (`select`, filters, `order`, `limit`, `range`, `single`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`) and resolve
  to `{ data, error, count, status }`; a prepare step writes each table's `Row` / `Insert` /
  `Update` types to `.denext/rest.ts` from the live catalog (a stub without a database). Guide:
  [Backend › Auto-REST](https://denext.dev/docs/backend#auto-rest).

### Changed

- **A channel's `onIdle` says why its key went idle.** `createChannel({ onIdle })` is now called
  with `(key, reason)`: `"disconnect"` when the last subscriber's connection closed (it may come
  back with the same key) and `"unsubscribe"` when it unsubscribed, was revoked or was denied on
  re-authorization. Re-subscribing to the same key under the same subscription id no longer takes
  the key through `onIdle` / `onActive`.
- **`@denext/backend`: `db()` reads the identity at each query.** Without `as`, who a `db()` client
  acts as is resolved for each query, from the request current when the query is made (once per
  request), not when the client was made — so a module-level `const sql = db()` serves every
  visitor as themself and is `anon` outside a request. `db({ as })` stays fixed.
- **`@denext/backend`: storage outside a request needs a service handle.** With no request there is
  no session to pass `authorize`, so a plain `storage.bucket(name)` call from a task or script is
  refused (`forbidden`, naming `{ service: true }`); a public bucket's downloads stay open. Use
  `storage.bucket(name, { service: true })` there.
- **`@denext/backend` auto-REST defaults.** `statementTimeout` is 5000 ms (was 8000); new
  `maxConcurrent` (default half the pool's `max`, else 5; excess requests wait up to 1 s, then get
  `503` `PGRST003` with `Retry-After`) and `exactCount` (`"authenticated"` by default: an anonymous
  `Prefer: count=exact` is refused with `400`; `"all"` / `"never"`).
- **`nativeBearerToken(request)`** is exported from `denext/server`: the `Authorization: Bearer
  nat_…` parser `auth()` uses, for handlers that exempt native-app requests from a cookie check.
- **`clientIpForLimits()`** is exported from `denext/server`: the address to key a per-address
  limit on — `clientIp()`, or `undefined` when that is an untrusted loopback, private, link-local
  or unique-local socket peer (a reverse proxy every visitor shares, so a limit on it would be
  site-wide).

### Fixed

- **`clientIp()` works inside Live hooks.** A channel's `authorize`, a `defineSubscription`
  resolver or `authorize`, `live.authorize` / `canJoinRoom` / `canSubscribe` / `canWatchTags`, a
  `useLive` fetcher and a `<Live>` re-render ran on a request rebuilt from the connection's cookie
  with no client address, so `clientIp()` returned `undefined` there. They now see the address
  `clientIp()` answered in the upgrade request: the socket peer, or the trusted proxy's last
  `x-forwarded-for` hop under `trustForwardedHeaders` / `DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`.
- **`@denext/backend` realtime: a timestamp key no longer loses its changes.** The re-read and
  seed queries returned the key as `t."key"::text` while the trigger's notification spells it
  `to_jsonb(row) ->> 'key'`; for a `timestamp` key the two differ (`2026-01-02 03:04:05` against
  `2026-01-02T03:04:05`), so a re-read row matched no notification and a seeded key matched no
  delete. Both queries now return the key the way the trigger does (`to_jsonb(t."key") #>> '{}'`,
  the same text without building a JSON document per row); the comparison stays in the column's
  own type, so the key index still serves it.

### Security

- **`denext ui`'s "Read as" preview ignores leftover per-claim settings.** It set only `role` and
  `request.jwt.claims`, so a `request.jwt.claim.sub` left on a pooled connection could make
  `auth.uid()` answer for another user in the preview. It now blanks those settings, as
  `@denext/backend` does.
- **Live connections are capped per client address.** `live.limits.maxConnectionsPerIp` (default
  64) refuses, with 429 before upgrading, a handshake from an address that already holds that many
  sockets — the address `clientIp()` answers (an IPv6 address counts as its /64). One client could
  otherwise take every one of `maxConnections`. The cap is off for a connection whose address is
  an untrusted loopback, private, link-local or unique-local socket peer (`127.0.0.0/8`, `10/8`,
  `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`, `169.254/16`, `::1`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`, and their IPv4-mapped
  forms): behind a reverse proxy without `trustForwardedHeaders` every visitor arrives from the
  proxy's address, so the cap would be site-wide. Such connections still count against
  `maxConnections`, and the server warns once that per-address limits are off until
  `trustForwardedHeaders` (or `DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`) is set; the first 429 from the cap is logged
  once too, naming the address and the option.
- **`@denext/backend` realtime: signed-out subscribers share one quota per address.** A signed-out
  subscriber's `maxSubscriptionsPerIdentity` and seed budget were per Live connection, so opening
  more sockets bought more of both. They are now per client address (`anon:<address>`, from
  `clientIpForLimits()`), falling back to the connection when the address is unknown or an
  untrusted proxy-looking peer.
- **`@denext/backend` realtime: one client can no longer fill an instance's subscriptions.** Each
  subscribe with a fresh key created a subscription (and ran a seed query of up to
  `maxTrackedKeys` keys) that was kept 15 s after its subscriber left, against one instance-wide cap
  of 10 000 with no per-subscriber limit, so a single signed-out client churning keys could hold
  every slot. Subscriptions are now capped per identity (`maxSubscriptionsPerIdentity`, default 64:
  a signed-in user across their connections, or one signed-out Live connection), an unsubscribed
  key is forgotten at once, one whose connection closed is kept for a reconnect only while there is
  room (at either cap the oldest such one gives way; only live subscriptions refuse a new one), and
  seed queries run at most four at a time within a per-identity budget (a burst of 32, then 8 a
  second).
- **`@denext/backend` realtime: re-reads use the table's indexes and cannot pile up.** The re-read
  and seed queries compared the key and the filter column as text (`t.id::text in (…)`), which no
  index serves, so every burst was a sequential scan per subscriber group, and bursts arriving
  while one ran started more in parallel. Keys and filter values are now cast to the column's own
  type, read once from the catalog (`t.id = any(array(…)::<type>)`, an index scan); each query runs
  under a transaction-local `statement_timeout` (`queryTimeoutMs`, default 5 000; a timed-out
  re-read is a `resync`); and flushes are single-flight, so bursts that arrive during one are
  delivered together by the next. Distinct filters (re-read groups) per identity are bounded by
  `maxSubscriptionsPerIdentity`.
- **`@denext/backend` auto-REST no longer exposes relations without row-level security by
  default.** With `tables: "*"` only tables (and partitioned tables) with RLS enabled and views
  created `with (security_invoker = true)` get a route; a granted table with RLS off, an ordinary
  (owner's-rights) view, a materialized view or a foreign table is skipped and listed, with the
  reason, in one startup warning. Naming a relation in `rest.tables` still serves it as named.
- **`@denext/backend` auto-REST can no longer exhaust the shared Postgres pool** (`maxConcurrent`,
  a shorter `statement_timeout`, and no anonymous exact counts by default — see Changed).
- **`@denext/backend` auto-REST CSRF exemption matches `auth()`.** Only a request whose
  `Authorization` header `auth()` itself reads as a native bearer session skips the cross-site
  check; a look-alike spelling (`Bearer<TAB>nat_…`) that left the session on the cookie no longer
  does.
- **`@denext/backend`: a `db()` client kept at module scope no longer keeps its first visitor's
  identity** (see Changed).
- **`@denext/backend` row-level security: legacy claim settings can't override the identity.** The
  setup statement also blanks `request.jwt.claim.sub`, `.role`, `.email` and `request.jwt.claim`
  transaction-locally (still one pipelined statement), so a value left on a pooled connection or
  set as a role default never wins over `request.jwt.claims` in Supabase's `auth.*` functions.
- **`@denext/backend`: custom claims can't set `email`.** `sub`, `role` and `email` are stripped
  from `rls.claims` and `db({ as: { claims } })`; `email` comes from the user alone.
- **`@denext/backend` storage fails closed outside a request** (see Changed).
- **`@denext/backend` S3 presigned downloads carry a content disposition.** Every presigned `GET`
  the plugin signs sets `response-content-type` to the stored type and
  `response-content-disposition` to `inline` only for raster images, audio, video, PDF and plain
  text (the object route's rule) and `attachment` otherwise, so an object a client uploaded but
  never completed (never sniffed) cannot render as HTML or SVG from the store's origin. The guide
  documents bucket lifecycle rules for uploads that were never completed.

## [3.4.14] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- **Docs: a Coming from Supabase guide.** `/docs/coming-from-supabase` maps each Supabase feature
  to denext and `@denext/backend` (with side-by-side snippets for queries under row-level security,
  sign-in, storage, realtime and edge functions), gives a migration checklist (schema and policies,
  users with their ids and bcrypt hashes, storage objects, environment) and lists what is not there
  yet.
- **`@denext/backend`: realtime from the database.** `backend({ postgres, realtime: realtime({ tables:
  { notes: { events?, key? } } }) })` opts tables in: migration `backend_realtime_0001` installs a
  trigger function, and one migration per table an AFTER … FOR EACH ROW trigger, that
  `pg_notify('denext_realtime', …)` with `{ table, op, key, old_key?, ts }` — keys only, never row
  data. One listening connection per server instance (`SqlClient.listen`, optional; `Deno.SQL` has
  it and `fromPostgresJs` maps postgres.js's) coalesces a burst within 16 ms; each subscriber's
  rows are re-read under their own row-level security, one query per identity per burst (a
  500-row transaction for two users: one flush, two re-reads). `useTableChanges(table, { initial,
  filter, key, onChange, onResync })` from `@denext/backend/client` keeps a row list live over the
  Live socket; a subscription key is bound to one identity, a delete reaches only subscribers who
  could see the row (tracked keys, seeded at subscribe), and a lost frame or reconnect marks it
  `stale`. On the server, `onTableChange(table, fn)` (keys, service context) and
  `tableChanges(table, { as, filter, onChange })` (RLS-scoped); `revalidate: true` calls
  `revalidateTag("table:<name>")` per burst. Without `listen` it throws
  `RealtimeUnsupportedError` (`code: "unsupported"`). Guide:
  [Backend › Realtime from the database](https://denext.dev/docs/backend#realtime-from-the-database).
- **Channel lifecycle hooks** (`denext/server`): `createChannel({ onActive, onIdle })` is told when
  a key gains its first or loses its last subscriber on this instance — where a channel releases
  per-key state. `SqlClient` gains an optional `listen(channel, fn, onlisten)` (`SqlListener`).
- **`denext ui`: a Database section** for a project that uses Postgres (`DATABASE_URL` is
  `postgres://`, or the config declares `postgres:`). Tables (row estimates, columns, keys,
  indexes, foreign keys); rows — 50 a page, keyset-paged on the primary key, sort, `column = value`
  filter, view, edit a value, insert, delete; row-level security policies, with an "as user"
  preview (`anon`, or a user id under the claims `db({ as: user })` sends) beside the clearly
  labelled service role; migrations (status, apply); `backend({ storage })` buckets and objects
  (download as an `octet-stream` attachment, delete); denext auth's users (sessions, MFA,
  passkeys; revoke sessions, delete). Every write is previewed as the exact SQL and its parameters
  first and works with JavaScript disabled; enabling RLS writes a migration rather than altering
  the table. The UI still runs no project code: each page asks a hidden `denext db-admin` child,
  which uses the project's own client and storage driver; every query runs in its own transaction
  with a statement timeout (reads `READ ONLY`), identifiers come only from `pg_catalog`, values
  are parameters, passwords are masked, and `--read-only` refuses every write in the server and
  again in the child. Guide: [Project UI › Database](https://denext.dev/docs/ui#database).
- **`@denext/backend`: realtime revalidation on one instance.** `realtime({ revalidate: { owner:
  "one" } })` has a single server instance per database call `revalidateTag("table:<name>")` per
  burst — the holder of a session-level Postgres advisory lock on a reserved connection, checked
  once per burst; when it stops or dies the next instance to see a burst takes over. For a cache
  shared by every instance; the default (`true`, `{ owner: "every" }`) stays one revalidation per
  instance. `SqlClient` gains an optional `reserve()` (`Deno.SQL` has it; `fromPostgresJs` maps
  postgres.js's), which the lock needs; without it every instance revalidates, with a warning.

### Changed

- **`@denext/backend`: a single `db()` query is one round trip on `Deno.SQL`** (was two): the
  scoped transaction hands the driver the role/claims setup and the query unstarted, as an array
  (`begin(tx => [setup, query])`), so `BEGIN`, both statements and `COMMIT` go out together. A
  failed setup still aborts the transaction before the query runs. The `SqlClient.begin` contract
  now states that a returned array is awaited as a whole (as `Deno.SQL` and postgres.js do); a
  client that does not is refused with a `TypeError` instead of running the query unscoped.

### Fixed

- **Reading task run history never changes the database.** `postgresTaskHistoryStore`'s `read()`
  and `listRuns()` no longer run the table migration: before the first recorded run they answer
  "no history recorded yet" (as the SQLite store does). `denext task --history --read-only` passes
  `readOnly: true` to the store's `read()` (new `TaskHistoryReadOptions.readOnly`) and refuses
  `--clear-history`; `denext ui --read-only` reads a custom store's history that way.

## [3.4.13] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- **Pluggable task run history** (`denext/server`): `tasks: { history: { store } }` takes any
  `TaskHistoryStore` (`record`, `read`, `listRuns`, `prune`, `clear`, optional `close`); the
  `.denext/tasks.db` file stays the default (`sqliteTaskHistoryStore`, behaviour unchanged, and
  `{ maxRuns }` is its cap), and `postgresTaskHistoryStore({ sql | url, schema, maxRuns, migrate })`
  keeps every replica's runs in one `task_runs` table. Recording still never fails or delays a run,
  whatever the store does. `denext task --history [--json]` / `--clear-history` read and clear
  through the configured store, and `denext ui`'s Cron page reads through the store API (the
  default file in-process, an app's own store through those commands). Guide:
  [Scheduled tasks › Where history is kept](https://denext.dev/docs/jobs#history-store).
- **Postgres everywhere** (`denext/server`): `postgresAuthAdapter({ sql | url })` meets the same
  `AuthAdapter` contract as `sqliteAuthAdapter` (the shared contract suite runs against a real
  server), with its `sessions` store, on a database every replica shares; `postgresSessionStore`,
  `postgresRateLimitStore` (auth lockouts shared across replicas) and `postgresCacheStore` (data and
  ISR page cache, `revalidateTag` / `revalidatePath` reaching every instance) take the same
  options. `url` opens `Deno.SQL`, the Postgres client built into denext's Deno runtime; on stock
  Deno pass `sql: fromPostgresJs(postgres(url))` with the npm `postgres` package (a `url` there
  throws `PostgresUnsupportedError`, `code: "unsupported"`). Tables are created by migrations on
  first use (`migrate: false` to apply them out of band; `schema` keeps them out of `public`).
  `migratePostgres(sql, { dir | migrations, dryRun })` and `postgresMigrationStatus` apply SQL
  migrations in name order, each in its own transaction under an advisory lock, recorded with a
  checksum in `_migrations`. `denext generate migration` writes Postgres SQL in a Postgres project,
  and the generated `tasks/migrate.ts` runs on Postgres when `DATABASE_URL` is a `postgres://` URL
  (`--payload '{"dryRun":true}'` / `'{"status":true}'` list instead of applying, on SQLite too).
  Guide: [Databases › Postgres](https://denext.dev/docs/database#postgres).
- **`@denext/backend`: row-level security, Supabase-compatible.** `db()` runs every query in a
  transaction that first sets the role (`authenticated` for the request's signed-in user, else
  `anon`) and `request.jwt.claims` with `set_config(…, true)` — transaction-local, so nothing
  survives on a pooled connection or behind pgbouncer — pipelined with the query (three round
  trips per scoped query). Supabase's `auth.uid()`, `auth.role()`, `auth.email()` and `auth.jwt()`
  read those claims, so existing policies (`using (auth.uid() = owner)`) apply as written; the
  claims have a Supabase access token's shape plus `rls.claims(session)`. The roles and functions
  come from migration `backend_rls_0001` on first use (or `rlsSetupSql(role)` for a DBA and
  `rls: { migrate: false }`). `db({ as: "anon" | user | session })` picks the identity outside a
  request (where `db()` is `anon`); `db.service()` is the unscoped connection. A `begin` inside
  `db().begin` is a savepoint (`SqlClient.savepoint`, optional, also mapped by `fromPostgresJs`).
  Guide: [Backend › Row-level security](https://denext.dev/docs/backend#row-level-security).
- **`@denext/backend`: Postgres.** `backend({ postgres: { url | sql } })` opens one client for the
  app (`DATABASE_URL` by default, closed on drain); `db()` from `@denext/backend/server` returns it,
  and `backendAuthAdapter()` puts `denextAuth`'s tables on it. On stock Deno the app still starts
  and `db()` explains what is missing. Guide: [Backend › Postgres](https://denext.dev/docs/backend#postgres).

## [3.4.12] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- **`@denext/backend` 0.1.0: storage.** A new first-party plugin, `backend({ storage })`: buckets
  declared in `denext.config.ts` with `public`, `maxBytes`, a `mime` allow-list (a declared raster
  image is sniffed from its first bytes) and `authorize({ session, op, key, bucket, request })`,
  which runs for every operation made inside a request with the `denextAuth` session and denies
  when absent. Drivers: `s3()` for AWS S3, Cloudflare R2 and MinIO (SigV4 on `crypto.subtle`, no
  SDK; presigned PUT/GET, multipart upload, ListObjectsV2 paging) and `fs({ dir })` for development
  and self-hosting (HMAC-signed, expiring URLs served at `/_denext/storage/`, `Range` downloads).
  `storage.bucket(name)` from `@denext/backend/server` signs uploads and downloads, uploads,
  downloads, heads, lists and removes; `uploadFile` (progress, multipart above a threshold) and
  `getFileUrl` from `@denext/backend/client` drive it from the browser through
  `POST /_denext/storage/sign`, which applies the `csrf()` rule and validates its body. Downloads
  can resize images (`transform: { width, height, quality, format }`). Guide:
  [Backend](https://denext.dev/docs/backend); example: `examples/backend-storage`.
- **`transformImageBytes(bytes, transform, { images, cacheKey })`** (`denext/server`): the
  `/_denext/image` pipeline for image bytes the caller already holds — the same codecs, SVG and
  decompression-bomb refusal, concurrency gate and output cache, with `width` / `height` bounded to
  `images.deviceSizes ∪ images.imageSizes`, the image fitted inside the box and never enlarged.
- **`parseRange(header, size)`** (`denext/server`): the single-range `Range` header parser the
  static file server uses, for handlers that serve bytes themselves (`undefined` = serve it all,
  `null` = 416).

### Fixed

- **Security: a request's context could leak into later code after a lazily loaded module.** The
  first `import()` of a module made during a request (an image codec on the first
  `/_denext/image` or storage transform, a route module, a wasm tool in dev) left that request's
  async context active afterwards: the next request the server dispatched, a scheduled task or a
  timer the module started could see `currentContext()` return the finished request, so a
  `cookies()` / `auth()` read or a storage `authorize` check could run with another user's
  session. Shared loaders (route and island modules, the image, OG, Sass, Lightning CSS, SWC and
  MDX tools, the cache store, task and instrumentation modules, content collections' store and
  MDX modules) now load outside the request, every request and scheduled run starts with no
  request context, and shared timers (Live and channel flushes, ISR background regeneration)
  start outside the request that triggered them.

## [3.4.11] - 2026-10-12

### Fixed

- **`denext desktop package` on macOS no longer reads as signing with `-` when
  `DENEXT_CODESIGN_IDENTITY` is set.** `deno desktop` seals every bundle it compiles, ad-hoc when
  deno.json names no identity, and logs `Codesigning bundle with identity "-"`; the package script
  then re-signs with the Developer ID, so the finished `.app` was right but the log looked wrong.
  The runtime has no switch to skip that pass (and the launch config written after it, or a
  universal merge, break its seal anyway), so `scripts/package-macos.ts` now says before the build
  that it is an ad-hoc pre-sign it re-signs with the identity, and names the identity on each
  re-sign. Regenerate an existing script with `denext desktop package --regenerate-scripts`.
- **The macOS package script's Developer ID re-sign keeps what `deno desktop`'s own signing pass set
  up.** The runtime signs every Mach-O in `Contents/MacOS` with the bundle's `CFBundleIdentifier`;
  the re-sign renamed the runtime library (`laufey.dylib`, `libruntime.dylib`) after its file, and
  it re-signed each nested helper and framework without `--preserve-metadata=entitlements`, so a
  CEF helper's entitlements would have been dropped. It now passes `--identifier` for the
  binaries beside the main executable and preserves nested code's entitlements (and the bundle's,
  when no `DENEXT_ENTITLEMENTS` / `desktop.macos.entitlements` replaces them). Checked on a
  Developer ID–signed CEF build: `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes and the renderer
  helpers start. Regenerate an existing script with `denext desktop package --regenerate-scripts`.
- **The pinned Intel-Mac (`x86_64-apple-darwin`) CEF runtime installs again.** Every Mach-O in that
  archive ships with no signature (Apple's linker signs arm64 code ad hoc, not x86_64), and the
  install's ad-hoc re-sign of `laufey.app/Contents/MacOS/laufey` failed with "code object is not
  signed at all / In subcomponent: …laufey Helper (Renderer).app", so CEF packaging on an Intel Mac
  stopped before it started. The install now ad-hoc signs unsigned nested code inside-out (the CEF
  framework's libraries, the framework, each helper app) before that re-sign; code that already
  carries a signature, as in the arm64 archive, is left alone.
- **A Developer ID–signed macOS app gets the entitlements V8 needs under the Hardened Runtime.** The
  package script signed the main executable (which hosts V8) and the CEF helpers with
  `--options runtime` but no entitlements unless `DENEXT_ENTITLEMENTS` /
  `desktop.macos.entitlements` supplied some, and the Hardened Runtime denies JIT code its
  executable memory without `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` (fatal for V8 on Apple Silicon). With
  an identity, the main executable is now signed with `allow-jit`,
  `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` and `disable-library-validation` (Deno's own release-signing
  set, `cli/entitlements.plist`, minus `allow-dyld-environment-variables` and
  `disable-executable-page-protection`), the CEF Renderer and GPU helpers with Chromium's
  `allow-jit`, and the Plugin helper with Chromium's `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` +
  `disable-library-validation`. Explicit entitlements get the main executable's keys merged in;
  a key they set, to `false` too, is kept. Without explicit ones the defaults join what
  `deno desktop`'s signing pass applied. New in `denext/desktop`: `V8_ENTITLEMENTS`,
  `cefHelperEntitlements` and `macosSigningEntitlements`. Regenerate an existing script with
  `denext desktop package --regenerate-scripts`.
- **An ad-hoc macOS re-sign no longer turns on the Hardened Runtime.** Without
  `DENEXT_CODESIGN_IDENTITY`, the package script's re-sign (after it writes the launch config, or
  after a universal lipo merge) still passed `--options runtime` but applied no JIT entitlements,
  so V8 in the main executable and the CEF Renderer / GPU helpers could be denied the executable
  memory their JIT needs on Apple Silicon. The ad-hoc re-sign now omits `--options runtime`, as
  `deno desktop`'s own ad-hoc signing pass does; only notarization needs the Hardened Runtime, and
  it needs a real identity. Regenerate an existing script with
  `denext desktop package --regenerate-scripts`.

## [3.4.10] - 2026-10-11

### Added

- **A module sidecar can start a child of itself.** A backend that re-runs its own entry with a
  subcommand (an MCP stdio bridge, an agent; Electron's `spawn(process.execPath, [script,
  "mcp-bridge"])` with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`) could not inside a `desktop.sidecars`
  `run: { module }` worker, whose `process.execPath` is the app. `globalThis.denextSidecar` now has
  `spawnSelf(args, options)` (a `node:child_process` child) and `childCommand(args)` (its
  `{ command, args, env, stdio }` for your own spawn): the app's executable runs again as a
  headless worker of the Deno Desktop runtime (no window, no web engine, no single-instance check),
  the entry's `runDesktop` runs that sidecar's module with `process.argv.slice(2)` = `args` and
  `denextSidecar.child === true` instead of a window, and the process ends with the module's exit
  code. The child has the app's baked permissions and nothing more, opens no listener, gets no
  secrets or bootstrap, and its stdout starts clean (the runtime's two start-up lines are
  removed). It needs the sidecar's `permissions.run` to cover the app's executable (`["*"]`, as
  its installed path is the user's). `runDesktop` resolves with `sidecarChild` set in a child.
  Docs: [Desktop › A child of the sidecar](https://denext.dev/docs/desktop#desktop-sidecars-children).

### Fixed

- **An island imported only through an import-map alias hydrates when the build runs from another
  folder.** The client-boundary and hydration crawls ran `deno info` in the caller's working
  directory, so Deno took the import map found there, not the app's: `denext build ./app`,
  `denext export ./app` or `denext dev ./app` run from a parent folder (and an in-process
  `build(dir)`) could not resolve `@/components/Counter.tsx` (`"@/": "./"`), missed the
  `"use client"` island behind it, and shipped the route as static HTML ("1 static route(s) ship no
  client JS") that never hydrated. The crawls now run in the folder of the app's `deno.json`, as
  Deno does for a command run in the project, on `build`, `export` and both dev loops. A build run
  inside the app folder (`deno task build`) was not affected.
- **A SPA's bundled dev loop serves each shell its own platform files.** Under
  `DENEXT_DEV_UNBUNDLED=0`, `denext mobile dev` / `denext desktop dev` against a SPA got the `web`
  build (entry bundle, stylesheet and `spa.shell`) whatever the session's target, while the
  unbundled loop and the App Router dev paths took each target's. The bundled loop now builds per
  target: a session whose platform files resolve unlike `web`'s (or that renders another
  `spa.shell`) gets a build of its own on its first request after an edit, kept beside `web`'s
  (`.denext/spa-dev/<gen>-<target>`), and a target with no files of its own shares `web`'s build.
- **A list pinned to its end keeps its last rows in view as Android shrinks the WebView.** Android
  (the Capacitor shell, and Chrome resizing content) resizes the WebView around the keyboard itself,
  before `keyboardWillShow`, so nothing covers the page and React Native mode's
  `KeyboardChatScrollView` / `KeyboardAwareLegendList` never lifted: the scroll view shrank with
  its scroll offset unchanged and its last rows went under the keyboard. Their keyboard lift now
  puts a list that was at its end (within 20 px) as the layout viewport shrank back at its end;
  a list scrolled away, an inverted one, `keyboardLiftBehavior: "never"` and a frozen lift are
  left alone.
- **An inverted list scrolled away from its end keeps its rows put as the iOS keyboard hides.**
  With `resize: "native"` / `"body"` / `"ionic"` the Capacitor shell grows the app back only
  after will-hide's animation, and the keyboard watch stopped at will-hide, so an inverted
  `KeyboardChatScrollView` that had not lifted (`keyboardLiftBehavior: "whenAtEnd"` away from
  its end) stayed scrolled past the resize's room and its rows jumped down by the keyboard's
  height when the shell grew back. The watch now outlives will-hide until the shell has grown
  the app back (at most a second), and such a list scrolls back as it does.
- **`denext dev` serves a next-compat app's shells their own platform files.** A compat drop-in
  App Router app's dev build (the esbuild server render, the client entries and the Flight
  islands) was built for `web` only, so `denext mobile dev` and `denext desktop dev` rendered
  and hydrated the `web` files while the native App Router path and SPA mode took each target's.
  Each target whose platform files resolve unlike `web`'s now gets a build of its own (its
  Flight boundary crawled through its files, its islands served for it, unbundled or bundled),
  built on the target's first request after an edit and kept beside `web`'s, so two shells on
  one dev server never rebuild each other's. A target with no files of its own shares `web`'s
  build, so an app without platform files builds once as before.
- **`reactCompiler` memoizes a component imported through an import-map alias.** Deno maps an
  alias (`@/components/Pane.tsx`) once, to the plain file, so the auto-memo compiler's output for
  a module imported that way was never bundled: an island importing `@/components/Pane.tsx` got
  the uncompiled `Pane`, whether or not the island was itself a copy made for a platform file
  (`denext build`, `export` and the bundled `denext dev` loop alike). The client bundles now
  rewrite such an importer's alias imports to the transformed module, through the copies they
  already make for platform files.

## [3.4.9] - 2026-10-11

### Fixed

- **A plain bottom-anchored scroll view keeps its last rows in view when the iOS shell resizes.**
  React Native mode's `KeyboardChatScrollView` and `KeyboardAwareLegendList` (their keyboard lift)
  treated the Capacitor shell's delayed resize as the keyboard closing: they scrolled the content
  back down as the WebView / `<body>` shrank, so a scroll view at its end hid its last rows behind
  the keyboard until the user scrolled. The room after the content now gives way to the shrunk
  scroll view without moving the content, and a scroll view whose end was in view (within 20 px) as
  the keyboard opened stays pinned to its end through the lift, the resize, a suggestion bar
  and the hide, until the user scrolls away from it.
- **`KeyboardAvoidingView`, `KeyboardStickyView` and React Native mode's keyboard views lift
  while the iOS keyboard slides in.** In the Capacitor shell with `resize: "native"` (the
  default), `"body"` or `"ionic"` they read the visual viewport, which `@capacitor/keyboard`
  keeps still, so they stayed put for the ~450 ms before the shell's delayed resize landed and
  the keyboard covered what they should have lifted. They now share `useKeyboardInset()`'s
  measurement: the will-show height (animated over the keyboard's 250 ms) less however far the
  shell has resized the WebView / `<body>` / `ion-app` since, so the lift drops at once as the
  resize lands and nothing is lifted twice.
- **A module sidecar no longer sees the worker's `location`.** A `desktop.sidecars` `run: { module }`
  backend runs in a `blob:` worker, whose `WorkerLocation` reads origin `"null"`, so a library that
  resolves URLs against `location.origin + location.pathname` (Effect's `Url.make`, behind every
  `HttpClient` request) built `nullnull/<uuid>/…` and every request failed with `Invalid URL`. The
  worker now hides `globalThis.location` before the module loads, as Node's main thread has none.
- **`secureStore`'s `fallback: "session"` takes only a genuine OS-store refusal.** Every rejection
  that was not a `TypeError` fell back to `sessionStorage`, so a desktop `validation` or `forbidden`
  error over the bridge, a bridge `timeout` or a programming error was swallowed into the not-secret
  copy. The fallback now covers the desktop capability's `backend_unavailable` / `store_failed` /
  `unavailable` and a rejection of the secure-storage plugin's own call other than its
  `missingKey` / `invalidData` usage errors; anything else rejects with its own error.

## [3.4.8] - 2026-10-11

### Fixed

- **A list pinned to its end keeps its last row above the iOS keyboard while the Capacitor shell
  resizes.** `@capacitor/keyboard` takes the keyboard's notifications away from WebKit, so the
  visual viewport never moves, and with `resize: "native"` (the default), `"body"` or `"ionic"` it
  resizes the WebView / `<body>` / `ion-app` only after the keyboard's animation plus 200 ms.
  `useKeyboardInset()` read 0 the whole time, so a bottom-anchored `VirtualList` (`anchor="end"`)
  given it as `keyboardInset` was covered while the keyboard slid in and jumped when the resize
  landed; the documented `useKeyboard().height` instead added the room on top of the resize (the
  last row ended a keyboard's height too high). In the iOS shell the inset now follows the
  plugin's will-show / will-hide: the keyboard's height while it covers the page, less however
  far the shell has resized the app since, so it drops to 0 as the viewport shrinks and the
  last row does not move (with `resize: "none"` it stays the keyboard's height). The lists
  and mobile guides now pass `useKeyboardInset()` to `keyboardInset`.
- **A SPA build folds `feature("KEY")` in plain `.ts` / `.mts` / `.js` / `.mjs` modules too.**
  The SPA's esbuild (compat) production build ran the fold only over `.tsx` / `.jsx` components,
  so a hook or store calling `feature()` kept the runtime call (still reading the configured
  value) and its untaken branch shipped. The fold now also covers the app's own plain modules
  that import `denext/feature`; any other module, and everything in `node_modules`, loads as
  before, untouched.
- **`secureStore.get(key, { fallback: "session" })` finds the session copy when the OS store reads
  `null`.** The copy a refused `set(…, { fallback: "session" })` left in `sessionStorage` was read
  only when the OS read REJECTED; a store that refuses writes but answers reads with "no such item"
  (the Capacitor plugin, a desktop keychain) resolved `null` and the value was lost. `get` with the
  fallback now answers from the copy when the OS store holds nothing for the key; a value the OS
  store holds still wins, a successful OS `set` clears the copy and `delete` clears both.
- **`feature("KEY")` in a plain `.ts` / `.mts` / `.js` / `.mjs` client module is folded at build.**
  The native App Router build folded only `.tsx` / `.jsx` sources, so a hook or store calling
  `feature()` kept the runtime call and its untaken branch shipped. The fold now covers every
  project module a client bundle can contain (the same client-graph set the `asyncContext` pass
  instruments, crawled once for both); a module only the server tree reaches reads the flag at
  runtime, as before.
- **`Sheet`'s grabber no longer shows the focus ring after a tap or a click.** The grabber is a
  button, so pointer focus drew the browser's outline around the pill. The sheet now installs a
  `[data-dnx-sheet-grabber]:focus:not(:focus-visible)` rule: keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`)
  still shows the ring, pointer focus does not.
- **Production client bundles no longer carry StrictMode's dev double-invoke or the
  `useDebugValue` recorder.** Both only act in development, yet the reconciler shipped the
  StrictMode boundary check, its second render pass and the debug-value recording in every
  build. They are now installed by the dev entries (`installDevtools`) and `denext/testing`, as
  the other dev-only diagnostics are, so a production bundle drops them: examples/hello's shared
  runtime is 237 B smaller (65,590 → 65,353 B raw). Development behaviour is unchanged; in
  production StrictMode stays a plain Fragment and `useDebugValue` a no-op.
- **A native-stack header shows a string `headerTitle` over `title`.** When a screen set both,
  React Native mode's `createNativeStackNavigator` drew `title`; React Navigation draws
  `headerTitle` (its `getHeaderTitle`), and so does denext now, in the bar, the iOS large title
  and the next screen's back label. `title` stays the screen's title for route announcements.
- **A native-stack screen with no `title` shows its route name in the header.** React Native
  mode's `createNativeStackNavigator` (and expo-router's `Stack`) drew an empty header when a
  screen set neither `title` nor `headerTitle`, and dropped a string `headerTitle`; the title now
  falls back to the string `headerTitle`, then the route name, as React Navigation does, and a
  `headerTitle` function gets that title as `children`.

## [3.4.7] - 2026-10-11

### Added

- **`secureStore` can fall back to `sessionStorage`, opt in per call.** `secureStore.set(key, value,
  { fallback: "session" })` and `secureStore.get(key, { fallback: "session" })` keep and read the
  value in the page's `sessionStorage` (under a namespaced key) when the OS store refuses, such as
  `backend_unavailable` from a locked or absent Linux keyring, and warn once with the reason. `set`
  now resolves `{ stored: "keychain" | "indexeddb" | "session" }` (it resolved `undefined`; callers
  that ignore it are unaffected). A later keychain `set` of the key clears the session copy and
  `delete` clears both. `sessionStorage` is NOT secret and ends with the tab; `requireBiometric`
  never falls back. Without the option nothing changes: a refusal still rejects.

### Changed

- **Touch and wheel handlers are dispatched from the root, as in React.** `onTouchStart`,
  `onTouchMove`, `onTouchEnd`, `onTouchCancel`, `onWheel` and their `Capture` variants now ride
  root event delegation like every other bubbling event: each root and portal container listens
  once (`touchstart`, `touchmove` and `wheel` passive, `touchend` / `touchcancel` not, as React DOM
  registers them), and an element with such a handler registers no listener of its own. So a
  `stopPropagation()` in one no longer stops the native event before the DOM listeners of the
  elements between it and the root, as with React's root listener. After `preventDefault()` in a
  passive handler (a no-op for the browser, in React too) the event now reports
  `defaultPrevented` and `isDefaultPrevented()` `true` for the rest of that dispatch, as React's
  synthetic event does; a native listener still reads the browser's own flag. Both differences
  are gone from KNOWN-DIFFERENCES.md.
- **Every app's shared client runtime is 1.8 KB smaller (raw), with no change in behaviour.**
  Dev Fast Refresh's per-render step (which implementation a component renders, the refresh-swap
  check and its hook-signature guard) and the per-module root refresh are installed by
  `enableFastRefresh`, so a production bundle carries neither. The client reconciler's long
  error texts ("Rendered more hooks…", "Maximum update depth exceeded…", an async component or a
  `memo()`'d class on the client) are installed with the dev warnings and by `denext/testing`; a
  production bundle throws `denext: error <code> in <Component>`, and the codes are listed on the
  Troubleshooting page. The AsyncContext `Variable` ships only in an `asyncContext` build, and the
  fiber extension spells each field name once. `examples/hello`'s shared chunks went from
  67,385 B to 65,590 B, and the build-smoke budget moves from 67,400 B to 67,100 B.

### Fixed

- **`denext migrate --desktop` no longer writes a redundant `desktop.denoFlags`.** It wrote
  `["--node-modules-dir=none", "--exclude-unused-npm"]` into the generated `denext.config.ts`;
  `denext desktop run | dev | package` add both flags themselves for any npm project. The agent
  guide (AGENTS.md, llms.txt) and the desktop guide no longer say a pnpm workspace needs them.
- **The desktop docs and `denext desktop` no longer tell a pnpm workspace to set `desktop.denoFlags`.**
  `denext desktop run | dev | package` printed a hint, and the desktop guide and the config
  reference said, that a pnpm workspace member (`nodeModulesDir: "manual"`) needs
  `denoFlags: ["--node-modules-dir=none", "--exclude-unused-npm"]` or `deno desktop` rewrites the
  root `package.json`. `deno desktop` already gets both flags for any project with a
  `package.json` or `node_modules`; the hint is gone and the docs say so.
- **A desktop package script run directly works in a pnpm workspace.** `deno run -A
  scripts/package-<os>.ts` resolved `denext/desktop`'s own npm build dependencies (the sidecar
  bundler's esbuild) in the app's `nodeModulesDir: "manual"` mode, where they are not, so the run
  failed and Deno rewrote the root `package.json` from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`denext desktop
  package` already ran the script with `--node-modules-dir=none`). The scaffolded scripts now load
  `denext/desktop` dynamically after re-running themselves once under `--node-modules-dir=none`,
  whatever the project's mode; `denext desktop package` tells them it already did. Existing
  projects pick this up with `denext desktop package --regenerate-scripts`.
- **denext no longer makes Deno rewrite a pnpm workspace's root `package.json`.** Deno 2.9 reads
  `pnpm-workspace.yaml` only to migrate it: when a process in a pnpm workspace member's manual
  `node_modules` cannot find an `npm:` package there, it writes a `workspaces` field into the root
  `package.json` and fails. The `deno run` of the CLI that denext starts itself (the export
  `denext mobile build` runs, the dev server behind `mobile dev` and `desktop dev`, `denext ui`'s
  children and a compiled binary's hand-off to the pinned CLI) loaded the CLI's own npm build
  dependencies (esbuild) that way. In a pnpm workspace those children now run with
  `--node-modules-dir=none`, as the tasks `denext migrate` writes already did; elsewhere their
  command line is unchanged. The migrating guide says the flag is needed only on the command you
  type.
- **`denext mobile build` replaces Capacitor's placeholder splash on its own.** It replaced the
  splash only together with a placeholder icon, so an app whose icon was already its own kept the
  Capacitor logo on its launch screen. Each of the two is now replaced while it is still the
  placeholder, the splash generated from the resolved icon on its background colour.
- **An Expo app icon computed in code is reported, with the fix.** denext never runs the app config,
  so an `icon` computed there (an imported constant) cannot be resolved, and the native app got a
  web icon or Capacitor's placeholder with only a note to say why. `denext migrate --from expo`
  (and `--check`), `denext mobile assets` / `build` and `denext mobile doctor --store` now say that
  the app config computes the icon, what stands in for it, and to set `mobile.icon` in
  denext.config.ts to the icon exported as a 1024×1024 PNG.
- **Every `denext mobile` message names the native files where `ios.path` / `android.path` put
  them.** The manual steps and warnings of `mobile add` (each native installer's, e.g. "set
  NSSupportsLiveActivities", and the capability plan's), `add-ota`, `mobile doctor`, `mobile dev` and
  `mobile build` still printed the default `ios/App/…` / `android/app/…` paths for a project that keeps
  its shells elsewhere. `mobile doctor`'s scan of the app's own sources skipped folders named `ios`
  and `android` wherever they were, and walked the native projects (and the export copied into them)
  when they lived elsewhere: it now skips the configured native folders by path. The `.gitignore`
  lines `denext migrate --enable-capacitor` / `--from expo` add for the native build outputs follow
  an existing capacitor.config's paths too, and `denext mobile --help` says that its paths are
  Capacitor's default layout.
- **React Native mode: `TextInput` and the stack header look like React Native.** A focused
  `TextInput` drew the browser's focus ring, and a long placeholder in a one-line `multiline`
  input (a text field) wrapped onto a clipped second line. react-native-web's `TextInput` now
  has React Native's outline as its base style (0 wide, `solid`: an app's `outlineWidth`,
  `outlineColor` or Tailwind `outline-*` class still draws one) and a one-line placeholder cut
  with an ellipsis. The native-stack header's back button and bar button items were the browser's
  link colour: they now honour `headerTintColor` and otherwise default as React Navigation's
  native-stack does, to the navigation theme's `colors.primary` on iOS and `colors.text` on
  Android. `denext/navigation`'s `ScreenOptions` gains `headerTintColor`.
- **React Native mode: keyboard-aware lists lift with the keyboard.** `KeyboardAwareLegendList`
  (`@legendapp/list/keyboard`) and `react-native-keyboard-controller`'s `KeyboardChatScrollView`
  ignored their keyboard props, so the keyboard covered the last rows in the iOS shell and
  in Safari. While the keyboard covers the page they now get that much room after their content
  (less `keyboardOffset` / `offset`) and move their content up with it as on a phone, per
  `keyboardLiftBehavior`: `"always"` lifts and drops back, `"whenAtEnd"` lifts only when the end
  was in view, `"persistent"` stays lifted when the keyboard hides, `"never"` only adds the room;
  `freeze` pauses it. The room renders before the scroll moves, so the lift is never clamped.
  It follows `denext/mobile`'s keyboard overlap, so a WebView that resizes around the keyboard
  is not lifted twice.
- **React Native mode: uniwind's `pixelRatio()`, `fontScale()`, `hairlineWidth()` and theme
  scoping work.** uniwind's Vite plugin runs a lightningcss visitor over the compiled Tailwind CSS;
  denext's Tailwind output never got it, so those functions reached the browser unresolved and a
  `ScopedTheme` subtree kept the root's theme. With `uniwind` installed, the compiled
  `tailwind.output` now gets that pass on every `denext dev` and `build` compile: `pixelRatio(n)`
  is `n` device pixels' worth of px (`--denext-pixel-ratio`, from resolution media queries),
  `fontScale(n)` is `n` px scaled with the root font size (`n * 1rem / 16`), `hairlineWidth()` is
  `1px / devicePixelRatio`, theme variables declared with `@variant <theme>` move to the theme's
  class, and theme-variant utilities apply inside `@scope (.theme) to (<the other themes>)`, so
  the nearest `ScopedTheme` wins (so a preview can draw each theme in its own colours). Both
  Tailwind's nested output and its `--minify` output are handled. `denext/build/css`'s `buildAppCss`
  takes the pass as `tailwind.postprocess` (the new `AppTailwind` type).
- **An `asyncContext` build no longer fails on a module that imports by a relative path.** The
  transform writes each client module it instruments into `.denext/asyncctx/`, and the copy kept
  the original's relative specifiers, so they resolved beside the copy: `denext build` and
  `denext export` of `examples/hello` with `asyncContext: true` failed with
  `Module not found ".denext/asyncctx/island.tsx"` (its `dynamic(() => import("./island.tsx"))`),
  and so did any instrumented module's relative static import, `export … from`, stylesheet, JSON
  or platform-file module. The copy's static imports and its `import()` calls written as a
  literal (a string, or a template literal with no substitutions) now name the module beside the
  original. `import.meta` and a non-literal `import(expr)` are left as written, as for the
  original module: the bundler follows neither, and the browser resolves both against the chunk.
- **`asyncContext` also instruments the plain `.ts` / `.js` / `.mts` / `.mjs` modules a client
  bundle contains.** Only `.tsx` / `.jsx` files were instrumented, so an `await` inside a
